title: sse-anchored-offset-fence-and-deferred-tool-ack-recovery
author: Maya Chen
description: Background: We observed a rare class of failures where interleaved SSE fragments combined with delayed function/tool-call sentinel events produced malformed partial JSON or reordered tool call deliveries to downstream adapters. This typically manifests when: (1) a large model response is fragmented across TCP frames with non-deterministic chunk boundaries, (2) a function-call sentinel (fn_call start/stop) arrives split across fragments, and (3) upstream retries/resends produce a late-arriving chunk that should have been anchored to an earlier sequence. Problem: the existing reassembly logic relied on a simple linear byte window and last-seen sentinel heuristics which allowed two problems: a) "offset drift" where a late fragment would be stitched without verifying an anchored epoch causing JSON seam corruption, and b) tool-call ordering regressions when an fn_call stop token was observed after the reassembly finished and the adapter had already dispatched a synthetic call. What this PR does: introduces an "anchored offset fence" that ties fragment assembly to an epoch anchor (per-stream checkpoint) and requires a fence-ack for out-of-window late fragments before they can mutate a previously emitted JSON span. Adds a deferred-tool-ack handshake between the SSE reassembler and the OpenAI compatibility adapter so that fn_call boundaries are not acknowledged to adapters until the reassembler proves post-facto continuity of the sentinel span. This reduces duplicate or out-of-order function/tool deliveries while preserving low-latency emission in the common case. Key changes: - Reassembler: anchored offset fence with epoch checkpoints and a lightweight sequence checksum used to validate late fragment grafting. - Adapter: deferred-tool-ack API: adapters can opt into a short-duration lease (configurable, default 30ms) where tool-call dispatch is held until the reassembler clears the fence or times out. - Metrics/tracing: new metrics sse.anchored_fence.* and tracing spans for fence_acquire/release, plus a debug-only reassembly digest for post-incident capture. - Backwards compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via compatibility flag openai.legacy_deferred_ack=false; enterprise customers can enable by default in their Private/Dedicated configs. - Tests: add deterministic fuzz harness and integration tests simulating split-sentinel, late-graft, and reordered-fragment scenarios. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4801 - [x] Unit tests for reassembler fences and checksums - [x] Integration tests for adapter handshake and timeout fallback - [x] Perf validation to confirm median latency impact < +3ms on streaming emits - [x] Metric and dashboard updates
commits: feat(sse): introduce anchored offset fence and epoch checkpoints
feat(adapter): add deferred-tool-ack interface and lease logic
test(sse): add fuzz harness and integration scenarios for split-sentinel
perf: microbenchmark reassembly path and tighten lock window
docs: explain deferred-tool-ack and compatibility flag

ci/perf - passed (median latency +2.1ms on streaming emit)
review_thread: Luis Ortega (2025-01-14): Can you clarify the conditions under which the fence drops fragments instead of grafting? We need deterministic behavior for audits.

Maya Chen (2025-01-15): Answered: the policy is 'verify checksum -> graft if ok; otherwise mark tombstone and emit a debug seam marker' — added unit tests to ensure tombstones are registered and prom metric increments.
Rupali Shah (2025-01-16): Suggests lowering default lease to 20ms for hosted to reduce impact on low-latency customers.
Maya Chen (2025-01-17): Updated default to 30ms and made hosted override via runtime config. Added perf microbench showing 30ms has <3ms P50 penalty; 20ms regresses P50 by ~6ms in our test workload.
Ben Greer (2025-01-19): Approves after nit on logging verbosity removed and added a debug-only trace flag.
discussion_notes: Design notes: The anchored fence trades a small window where emission can be deferred for correctness in rare split/sync cases. We avoid global stalls by scoping fences per-stream and per-epoch. The checksum is intentionally weak (rolling xor+len) to be cheap; if incidents require stronger validation we can upgrade to a lightweight CRC. Backoff/fallback: if the fence does not clear within lease timeout, the adapter will emit the best-effort event and mark it with sse.reassembly.fallback=true to allow downstream causal reconciliation.
testing_summary: Added 12 unit tests and 5 deterministic integration tests covering: split sentinel across three fragments, late graft within epoch, late graft beyond epoch (tombstone), function-call stop after reassembly, and adapter timeout fallback. Fuzz harness found two edge cases which are fixed: missing final newline causing sentinel ambiguity (fixed by newline-normalization prepass) and double-escaped delimiters (fixed by normalizing escape runs).
metrics_and_dashboards: New metrics: sse.anchored_fence.acquire_total, sse.anchored_fence.release_total, sse.anchored_fence.tombstone_total, sse.deferred_tool_ack.acquired, sse.deferred_tool_ack.timed_out. Dashboard included at metrics/dashboards/sse_anchored_fence.json for oncall. Alert: fire if tombstone_total / reassembly_attempts > 0.01 over 5m.
compatibility_and_rollout: Feature gated under openai.legacy_deferred_ack flag. Gradual rollout plan: enable for internal staging first (2 days), then for all hosted-rc customers with monitoring enabled (3 days), then default on Dedicated/Private after customer opt-in window. Migration note: older adapters that do not implement the deferred ack will continue to receive events as before; the reassembler will default to backward-compatible immediate ack mode if adapter does not register the lease.
release_notes: Fixes reassembly-induced partial JSON/structured-output corruption and prevents duplicate/out-of-order function/tool call deliveries by adding an anchored offset fence and a deferred-tool-ack handshake. Opt-in under openai.legacy_deferred_ack; recommended for customers experiencing split-sentinel errors.
merge_commit_message:
sse: anchored offset fence + deferred tool ack (fix partial-json and out-of-order tool calls)

Summary: introduce epoch-anchored reassembly fences and a short deferred-ack lease between the reassembler and OpenAI-compat adapter to prevent split-sentinel partial JSON and function-call reorderings. Includes tests, metrics and docs.
post_merge_actions: - Deploy reassembler + adapter change to staging cluster and enable openai.legacy_deferred_ack=true for 48h. - Add temporary e2e smoke in canary pipeline to exercise split-sentinel flows. - Monitor sse.anchored_fence.tombstone_total and sse.deferred_tool_ack.timed_out closely for first 72h.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report stalled streaming emits, check sse.deferred_tool_ack.acquired vs timed_out. If timed_out spikes, consider lowering lease in hosted runtime or enabling immediate-emit fallback for the affected tenant. Use debug trace to inspect reassembly digest for incident triage.
